query: How can educators improve learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: key_satisfaction_factors
per_column.rationale: Extracts the salient drivers/friction points from each open response, giving a groupable axis directly tied to 'how to improve satisfaction'. Values in the samples (technical_support, creativity_household_materials, asynchronous_flexibility_multimedia) are sound readings of the source text. The vocabulary is extremely fragmented (many near-unique compound labels), which weakens grouping leverage somewhat, but it still offers genuine thematic content.

per_column.name: primary_barrier
per_column.rationale: Naming the main obstacle is directly relevant to improving satisfaction and provides a compare/model axis. Sample values (technical_issues, disengagement, none) are well grounded in the text; NULL for silent rows is acceptable. However the very high NULL count (96) plus highly fragmented labels reduce practical leverage, and 'technical_issues_personalization' for ED-0003 slightly overreaches but is still defensible from the text.

per_column.name: innovation_present
per_column.rationale: A clean, low-cardinality yes/partial/no flag that partitions the data well and is useful for correlating innovative practice with satisfaction. Sample assignments are reasonable (kitchen-chemistry=yes, frozen algebra whiteboard=no), though 'innovation' is a mild inference on borderline rows; still warranted by the text.

per_column.name: engagement_quality
per_column.rationale: An ordinal engagement scale is a strong new analytical axis distinct from the numeric satisfaction score, enabling grouping and modeling on a dimension central to the query. Sample gradings align with the text tone (silent muted juniors=low, kids show up ready=high, crying second grader=very_low). Some subjectivity but clearly warranted.

judge.rationale: All four columns give genuine, non-redundant axes (thematic factors, barriers, an innovation flag, and an engagement scale) that materially support answering how educators can improve satisfaction; none merely restate the existing satisfaction score. Values in the row evidence are sound readings of the open responses, with appropriate NULL/none handling for silent rows and no invented facts. Main limitation is the heavy label fragmentation in the two free-text-derived columns, which lowers—but does not negate—their grouping leverage.
